Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout. Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` (integration-test-revert-verify §A8). The harness drives BOTH halves of the subject in one output: the new axes (J*) and req 675cb0ab's own suite (K*), because the authored half is not 'a neighbour not to break' — it is the second half of what this change decides, and K13 is its sharpest axis. ⛤ M4 is an ОБЪЯВЛЕННЫЙ НОЛЬ (expect []) and carries the mandatory `_canary`: the conjunct it removes is provably an identity, so a red set is not available for it.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/GroundingExecutor.ts

M1_discriminator_never_fires._note: The defect as it shipped: a substituted value is handed to updateProperty verbatim, so user text carrying ' #' / ': ' is truncated or breaks the frontmatter. Everything else must stay green — in particular the authored half (J3 / J4 / K13 / K14), whose pre-change shape this mutant restores, and J5, whose live shapes need no quoting either way.

M2_discriminator_always_fires._note: The reverted obvious fix, reached from the other side: with origin ignored, an AUTHORED flow array is serialised and quoted on its leading `[`, which is exactly the measurement that killed the first attempt. J4 / K14 stay green because a pre-quoted wikilink is a COMPLETE double-quoted scalar and needsYamlQuoting passes it through — that is why the last Gherkin scenario of req 675cb0ab holds unconditionally rather than by luck. J7 / J8 stay green because the other two conjuncts, not this one, hold them.

M3_obvious_fix_serialise_inside_the_tern._note: Byte-for-byte the attempt the issue records as implemented-measured-wrong-and-reverted. It reddens the authored half (J3 / K13) AND the ordering axis (J6): serialising before the guard quotes a bare `[[uid]]` on its leading `[`, isUnquotedWikilink stops seeing it, and req 29e0d1b6's loud refusal becomes a successful write. Three reds, one concern — the mutation is the whole wrong design, not one guard (integration-test-revert-verify §A139).

M4_string_semantic_conjunct_removed._note: ОБЪЯВЛЕННЫЙ НОЛЬ (integration-test-revert-verify §A135): zero reds is the CORRECT outcome and it is declared, not discovered. The conjunct is provably an IDENTITY, not a guard: on a string-semantic property the branch above has already applied serializeYamlScalar(v, true), whose rule is STRICTLY STRONGER than the plain serializeYamlScalar(v) this step would add — if the first pass quoted, its output is a complete double-quoted scalar and the second pass returns it verbatim; if the first pass left the value bare under the stronger rule, the weaker rule leaves it bare too. The conjunct is kept for a different reason than correctness: it keeps ONE step responsible for one property. The canary names a mutant of this same spec that MUST redden, so a zero here cannot be confused with a harness that stopped delivering the mutation.

M5_typing_conjunct_removed._note: Unlike M4 this conjunct IS load-bearing, and the arithmetic says why: the typed branch emits a canonical NEGATIVE integer BARE (that is the whole point of ticket 534a7a46), and a second, range-LESS pass quotes it on its leading `-` — re-introducing the sh:datatype violation that ticket removed. K8 / K12 stay green: they drive create_instance and an authored literal, neither of which carries a substitution.

M6_serialisation_moved_before_the_guard._note: Isolates the ORDER from the discriminator: the gate still decides correctly, only the guard now judges the SERIALISED form and so never fires on a substituted bare wikilink. Type-preserving (§A36) — serializeYamlScalar is already imported in this file and returns string. One red, exactly the ordering axis: K13 stays green because a quoted flow array is not `^\[\[…\]\]$`, so no refusal is raised and the written value is unchanged.
